findings.description: T4's FR-2 test description specifies that a test-only fulfilment stub 'raises on its first invocation' for a given provider_event_id, and D5/the Proposed design's orchestration step 3 establish that PaymentService.process_callback re-raises that exception uncaught (after releasing the claim) — meaning the test's first controller.handle()/process_callback call for that event will itself raise. Neither the FR-2 traceability row nor T4's task description nor the T4 bullet in 'Proposed design' states that the test must wrap that first call in assertRaises (or an equivalent try/except) before proceeding to the successful retry call. An implementer following the written specification literally could write the first call unguarded, causing the test to error out at that line instead of reaching the retry/verification steps the rest of T4 describes.
evidence: planning/plan-r3-c1.md, 'Functional requirement / constraint traceability' table, FR-2 row (Verification column: no mention of assertRaises/try-except around the first, failing call)

planning/plan-r3-c1.md, 'Proposed design', 'FR-2 test verification technique (T4)' bullets (describes stub behaviour and the post-retry assertions, but not how the test consumes the exception from the first call)
planning/plan-r3-c1.md, 'Proposed design', Orchestration step 3 and Design Decision D5 (fulfilment failure 're-raises the original exception unchanged' after release_for_retry() runs)
planning/plan-r3-c1.md, Implementation tasks table, T4 row (same omission)
findings.plan_section: Functional requirement / constraint traceability — FR-2 row; Implementation tasks — T4; Proposed design — 'FR-2 test verification technique (T4)'
findings.required_action: Optional, non-blocking: add one sentence to the FR-2 traceability row or the T4 'Proposed design' bullet stating that the test wraps the first (claimed-then-failing) call in assertRaises (or try/except) to consume the re-raised exception before issuing the retry call, so the verification technique is as fully specified as the rest of T4 already is.

review.summary: Independently re-verified round 3 against the raw JIRA/CONF:4812/CONF:4934 sources (re-read in full), the validated Planning Context, the current repository baseline (repository.py, payment_service.py, callback_controller.py, test_payment_service.py all re-read directly), the planning-workflow contract, and governance policy. Provenance is sound: every acceptance criterion, functional requirement, and constraint in the normalized context traces verbatim in substance to its cited raw source, with no invented, weakened, or contradicted requirement found, and the context's contradictions/open_questions/scope.uncertain arrays are legitimately empty (confirmed by direct re-read of all three raw documents). The round-2 review's sole PLAN_CHANGE_REQUIRED finding (PLAN-001: the FR-2 'exactly one row exists' assertion was unimplementable with the methods this plan actually adds to PaymentRepository) is genuinely resolved: this revision adopts exactly the reviewer's suggested option (b) — the FR-2 test proves row presence indirectly via a third record_if_new() call returning False — and the underlying logic is sound (PRIMARY KEY guarantees at most one row per provider_event_id; record_if_new() returning False is only possible if a row exists; together these are conclusive, not merely suggestive, proof), with no new PaymentRepository read/introspection method added, consistent with C-3's reuse bias. The core mechanism (gate fulfilment on record_if_new()'s boolean return; delete-then-reinsert release via a new release_for_retry(), never a status column, per C-4; unchanged controller response shape per AC-2/FR-4; barrier-synchronized genuine-concurrency test for FR-3/C-5) correctly implements every AC/FR/constraint and matches the repository baseline as independently confirmed by reading the current code. D1-D6 are all accurately grounded in either the validated context (D1, D2) or a genuine repository-evidence gap requiring a test-strategy choice the context is silent on by design (D3-D6), none of which rises to a blocking human decision. One non-blocking test-specification gap survives (below); it does not affect correctness of the design.
